channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review of 16 studies (n=3522) found ACLR patients had lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = -0.33), peak knee adduction angle (SMD = -0.47), and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = -0.64) during walking compared to controls. Delayed reconstruction (≥12 months) was associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, while early surgery (within 6 months) had fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but some temporary frontal-plane asymmetries and extension deficits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: A 6-month prospective cohort study (n=112) of stroke patients found stride time variability (STV) at discharge to be the only independent predictor of post-discharge falls. An optimal STV cutoff of 3.40% yielded an AUC of 0.756 (95% CI 0.657-0.851), with 88.2% sensitivity and 53.8% specificity for fall prediction.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 studies with 348 patients found that Action Observation Therapy significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.86), activities of daily living (SMD = 0.67), naming aphasia (SMD = 0.53), and motor function (gait velocity SMD = 0.70, TUG SMD = -1.05) in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Network-Based Brain Stimulation: Targeting the Frontoparietal Network for Cognitive Rehabilitation After Stroke Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs found non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) targeting the frontoparietal network in stroke survivors yielded moderate improvements in executive function (Hedges' g = 0.48), working memory (g = 0.41), and attention (g = 0.38). Combining NIBS with cognitive training showed superior outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of the timing and setting of pulmonary rehabilitation on functional recovery after lung cancer surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (1137 patients) found late-phase pulmonary rehabilitation significantly improved 6-min walk distance (MD = 68.86 m, 95% CI 53.46-84.26) and VO2peak (MD = 2.62 ml/kg/min, 95% CI 2.08-3.15) after lung cancer surgery. Early in-hospital rehabilitation showed no significant short-term benefits. Fully and partially supervised modes did not differ significantly in 6MWD.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Impact of Adding Fatigue-Focused Cognitive Behavior Therapy to Supervised Pilates-Based Core Stability Training on Balance and Walking in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: Adding fatigue-focused CBT to Pilates-based core stability training significantly improved balance and gait in multiple sclerosis patients, with a between-group mean difference of -0.59 in overall stability index (95% CI: -0.70 to -0.48; p < .001) and 8.22 steps/min in cadence (95% CI: 4.40 to 12.04; p < .001) after 8 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb motor recovery in people with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies (8 independent cohorts) found that self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb recovery in stroke patients showed no significant advantage over other interventions (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), but may offer comparable functional benefits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
item.description: A randomized crossover trial found that virtual reality (VR) and screen-based augmented reality (AR) feedback during robot-assisted gait training acutely and differentially modulated paretic muscle activation, limb loading, and propulsion-related mechanics in chronic hemiparetic stroke, with sequential combined VR + AR producing the broadest acute modulation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials found that low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome, with pulsed mode superior for analgesia and continuous mode for grip strength, and improved SNCV (Hedges' g=0.377, P=0.016).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Inertial measurement unit-based gait analysis for objective assessment of vestibular rehabilitation.
item.description: An IMU-based gait analysis during timed 25-ft walk tests in 30 acute vestibular syndrome patients showed significant improvements in vertigo-balance symptoms and gait parameters like walking speed, Gait Profile Score, and cadence after 6-week rehabilitation, even with a single pelvis sensor.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapy and Exercise-Based Rehabilitation for Mental Health: A Two-Decade Bibliometric Analysis of Global Trends, Thematic Evolution, and the Socioeconomic Vulnerability Gap (2006-2025).
item.description: A bibliometric analysis of 5223 publications (2006-2025) found a 22.6-fold increase in research on physical rehabilitation and mental health, predominantly from high-income countries (75.9%), with socioeconomic vulnerability remaining an under-researched theme (4.6% of publications explicitly referencing it).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Client Challenge
item.description: A three-arm RCT (n=48) found that both suspension core training and pressure biofeedback-guided core training significantly reduced pain and disability in chronic mechanical low back pain patients after four weeks compared to an advice-only control. Suspension core training showed additional benefits over pressure biofeedback in lumbar extension ROM and core muscle endurance, but not in pain intensity or flexion ROM.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: The clinical reasoning associated with prognosis and musculoskeletal disorders - A Masterclass in incorporating prognostic reasoning into physiotherapy practice.
item.description: This masterclass article outlines a practical framework for physiotherapists to incorporate clinical reasoning associated with prognosis into their management of musculoskeletal disorders, aiming to optimize patient outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: 3D Biomechanics of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries in Football: What We Have Learned in the Last Five Years.
item.description: A review of 33 cases of ACL injury in elite male football players revealed that ACL injury mechanics involve multiplanar knee rotations, with knee flexion increasing, a knee abduction shift, and a sequence of internal then external rotation of the femur. Whole-body postures leading to injury showed marked inter-individual variability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exploratory analysis of the impact of age stratification on outcomes of combined Salter osteotomy and femoral osteotomy in pediatric developmental dysplasia of the hip using a 3-year cutoff.
item.description: A retrospective study of 65 pediatric DDH patients found that those under 3 years old undergoing combined Salter and femoral osteotomy had superior radiographic improvements and significantly more excellent functional outcomes (Severin 97.1% vs 74.2%, P = 0.002) and lower avascular necrosis risk (0% vs 12.9%, P < 0.05) compared to older children.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Patients treated with rehabilitation alone after anterior cruciate ligament injury display greater muscle strength symmetry, yet lower absolute muscle strength normalized to bodyweight compared to reconstruction: A Cross-sectional study of 3,093 patients.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 3,093 patients with ACL injury found that those treated with rehabilitation alone (n=386) had greater muscle strength symmetry but lower absolute strength normalized to body weight compared to those who underwent reconstruction (n=2707).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative diagnostic utility of SPECT-CT versus MRI and CT in chronic low back pain.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study (n=122) found SPECT-CT positivity was moderately associated with Modic changes, advanced Pfirrmann grade, and vacuum disc/facet phenomena on MRI/CT in chronic low back pain, but structural and metabolic findings were frequently discordant (e.g., 60.7% of Pfirrmann 4-5 levels were SPECT-EP-negative).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Aqua Steps: A Feasibility Study of a new Aquatic Exercise Therapy Intervention for Falls Prevention in Older Adults.
item.description: A feasibility study (n=101) for the Aqua Steps aquatic exercise intervention in older adults at high falls risk demonstrated high feasibility, retention (88%), adherence (90%), and safety. It also showed preliminary reductions in falls (38%), fallers (36%), and frequent fallers (58%), with significant improvements in functional (22-70%), strength (10-80%), falls efficacy (11%), and balance confidence (8%) tests, sustained at 6-month follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Injury risk and physical therapy utilization following knee surgery in U.S. Army soldiers: a comparison of military and non-military treatment facilities.
item.description: A retrospective cohort study of 4924 US Army soldiers found that those undergoing knee surgery at non-military treatment facilities had higher subsequent injury rates (OR = 1.22, 95% CI [1.04-1.44]) and longer physical therapy duration (8.3 vs. 7.1 weeks) compared to those treated at military facilities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: VRCycle: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating a Virtual Reality Cycling Intervention in People With Knee Osteoarthritis.
item.description: A feasibility RCT with 41 knee osteoarthritis patients found that VR-enhanced cycling was highly feasible and acceptable, with both VR and traditional cycling groups showing improvements in pain and function after 6 weeks.
item.author: PubMed
